skill.name: only-what-was-asked
skill.description: Load before changing anything LIVE for a client or a business: pausing or turning on ads, campaigns or ad sets, changing budgets, turning off an app, bot, number or automation, cancelling a scheduled post, editing a live site, or any rule or script that can switch things off by itself. Use it for "only pause X", "just turn off Google Ads", "don't touch anything else", "solo le pausas", "solo eso", "no le apagues nada", "ni lo demás", "no toques lo demás", "sin tocar nada más", "que no apague nada". It pins the exact target (which client, which account, which channel, which object), writes the list of what must stay as it is, takes a before snapshot of both, changes only the target, then reads back the target AND the neighbours to prove nothing else moved, and checks that no automation will do more later. Not for code refactors in a repo (use a code blast-radius skill) and not for deciding whether to pause something.
skill.summary: Keep live business changes within the requested scope through target identification, state snapshots, verification, and automation checks.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

The skill requires verification and owner authorization before expanding changes. No evidence found of malicious reconnaissance, data exfiltration, or audit-directed prompt injection.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 restricts changes to the named target and requires checking that unrelated state remains unchanged. This is scope control, not reconnaissance.
Line 26 identifies the client, platform, account, object, and requested action before modification. The surrounding instructions require clarification rather than guessing ambiguous targets.
Line 41 prohibits changing protected items for unrelated business reasons and directs concerns to the owner. It limits authority rather than gathering system intelligence.
Line 72 is a sample report describing an automation disabled under the owner's order. Line 64 explicitly requires that authorization before disabling automation.
Line 77 forbids pausing everything unless the request explicitly covers everything. This prevents unauthorized scope expansion and contains no reconnaissance instruction.

content.user_title: Keep Live Changes Within the Requested Scope
content.value_statement: Small changes to live business systems can affect unrelated services or trigger later automation. This skill defines the target, preserves neighboring state, and verifies results.
actual_capabilities: Defines the client, platform, account, object, and action before a live change.
Creates a named do-not-touch list with current states.
Requires before snapshots and independent verification of the target and protected items.
Directs the agent to choose the smallest requested change and decline bundled changes.
Checks relevant automations and requires owner authorization before disabling them.
Structures a completion report with changed items, verified unchanged items, automation status, and access gaps.
limitations: Provides procedural instructions, not platform connectors or executable automation.
Does not decide whether pausing a service is the correct business decision.
Cannot verify protected items without access; those items must be reported as not checked.
Platform delays and cascading changes require platform-specific review and may require further approval.

use_cases.title: Pause One Advertising Campaign
use_cases.description: Pause a named campaign while checking that other campaigns, advertising channels, and client services remain unchanged.

use_cases.title: Cancel One Scheduled Post
use_cases.description: Cancel the requested post, record neighboring schedules, and verify that other scheduled content remains intact.

use_cases.title: Review Automatic Service Suspension
use_cases.description: Identify rules that could suspend client services, report previous actions, and change automation only within the owner's authorization.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Target
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a target statement for pausing [campaign] in [account] for [client] on [platform]. Ask about missing details before making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: clarify a single live change.

prompt_templates.title: Define Protected Items
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan to cancel [scheduled post] for [client]. List protected posts and channels, then specify snapshots and verification checks. Do not execute yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a scoped change plan.

prompt_templates.title: Execute and Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Pause only [campaign] in [account]. Snapshot protected items, make the smallest change, verify states, and report access gaps or unexpected differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: perform an authorized change with verification.

prompt_templates.title: Review Future Automation Effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Review automations affecting [client]. Report suspension triggers and previous actions. Propose notify-only behavior; do not disable rules or restore services without explicit authorization.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess delayed effects and authorization boundaries.

output_examples.input: Pause only Search MX for Client A in the specified Google Ads account. Leave Meta and the client app unchanged.
output: Paused: Client A, Google Ads, Search MX; previously active.
Verified unchanged: Meta ads active with three ad sets; client app on; other campaigns unchanged.
Automation review: no additional action authorized; any suspension rules require a separate decision.

output_examples.input: Review the client's automatic suspension rule. Do not change the rule or restore previously suspended services.
output: Found: an admin-console rule suspends services after six unpaid days.
Rule unchanged: disabling it was not authorized.
Previous suspensions: not checked because historical action logs were unavailable.
Decision required: retain the rule or authorize notify-only behavior.

best_practices: Confirm exact account and object identifiers before acting.
Record protected states before changes and compare them using the platform's current list view afterward.
Report inaccessible items and require authorization for automation changes or cascading effects.
anti_patterns: Pausing other channels because they belong to the same client.
Treating a confirmation message as proof that protected items remained unchanged.
Disabling automation or restoring previously affected services without the owner's authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to advertising platforms?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow for an agent using separately available tools and authorized platform access.

faq.question: Does it decide whether a campaign should be paused?
faq.answer: No. It controls the scope and verification of an authorized change, not the business decision.

faq.question: What happens when the target is ambiguous?
faq.answer: The workflow requires a short clarification question listing the options before any change.

faq.question: Can it disable automatic suspension rules?
faq.answer: Only when the owner's order covers that change. Otherwise, it reports the rule and leaves it unchanged.

faq.question: What happens when a protected item cannot be checked?
faq.answer: The report must mark the item as not checked and explain why. It must not claim that all protected items were verified.

faq.question: Is this intended for code refactoring?
faq.answer: No. The source excludes repository refactoring and focuses on live business systems, services, and automation.
